document.title: How to make a Part 36 offer and when can one be made?
document.summary: This guide summarises what a Part 36 offer is, when it can be made, who can make it and the requirements for a valid offer.

section.heading: What is a Part 36 offer?
section.para: A Part 36 offer is an offer of settlement that can be made by a party to settle all or part of a claim. The purpose of Part 36 is to encourage the parties to make or accept realistic offers. There are financial incentives for the offeror and risks for parties who turn down reasonable Part 36 offers. The claimant and defendant can both make Part 36 offers.

section.heading: When can a Part 36 offer be made?
section.para: A Part 36 offer can be made at any time, including prior to the commencement of court proceedings. Note, CPR 36 has no application in small claims track matters. The parties may make Part 36 offers limited to individual issues. The court may take into account any admissible offers when exercising discretion as to costs.

section.heading: Who can make a Part 36 offer?
section.para: Any party to a claim can make a Part 36 offer, whether they are a claimant, defendant, Part 20 claimant or Part 20 defendant. An appellant or respondent in appeal proceedings can also make a Part 36 offer. The judgment of the court will determine the outcome where an offer is not accepted.
